sections.title: Getting Started
sections.blurb: LogCore is your private, self-hosted life operating system. Everything you add lives in your own Brain (plain files you own), and an AI layer can read it and help you act on it.
howto: Use the left sidebar (or the bottom bar on your phone) to move between modules like Tasks, Notes, Calendar, and Chat.
Set your life priorities in Profile — LogCore uses them to score your tasks so the most important ones rise to the top.
Open Chat and just talk to your AI: ask it to plan your week, add tasks, or explain any feature.
Pin the modules you use most to the bottom bar (phone) in Settings → Shortcuts.
Every module page has an ⓘ button next to its title — tap it to jump straight to that module's help.

Click the 🔍 search icon in the header (or press Ctrl/Cmd+K) to search across your whole app at once — tasks, notes, goals, contacts, assets, calendar, finance, and journal — instead of hunting through each module separately.
tips: Not sure where something belongs? Ask the AI in Chat — it knows every module and will point you to the right one.
Your data never leaves your server unless you explicitly export or share it.
In the search bar, filter by tag alongside your search text — tags are shared across every module they exist on, so tagging something once makes it findable everywhere.

sections.title: Personal vs Business
sections.blurb: LogCore keeps your personal life and your business fully separated into two workspaces, each with its own data, modules, and priorities.
howto: If you have both, a toggle pill appears in the sidebar — switch between Personal and Business anytime.
Each workspace has its own tasks, calendar, notes, finance, contacts, and shared pool (Household vs Team).
Modules can differ per workspace — Journal, Household, and Home Assistant are personal; Team is business.
Your AI chat and priorities are scoped to the workspace you're currently in.
tips: Nothing crosses between workspaces automatically by default — that separation is the whole point — but an individual dashboard can be explicitly flagged to show up in both, from that dashboard's own ⚙ Settings.
An admin decides which workspaces you have access to.

sections.title: Sharing & Permissions
sections.blurb: Assets, Finance, Contacts, and Notes all share the same model: you decide who sees what, and at which level.
howto: Pick an access level: Read (view), Contribute (limited add/edit), or Edit (full, including re-sharing).
Sharing something personal sends the other person a request — they Accept or Decline from their notification bell.
Shared pool items (Household/Team) don't need a handshake since the pool is already visible to the group.
"Hidden from" excludes specific people (or a whole role) and always beats a share.
tips: Contribute access is configurable — for example, an employee who can only submit expenses, with no view of balances.
A rule targeting someone by name overrides any group- or role-level rule for them.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.blurb: LogCore reaches you through an in-app inbox (the bell), self-hosted push via ntfy, and web push on your devices.
howto: Click the bell to see your notification inbox; actionable items (like share requests) have Accept/Decline right there.
Enable browser/web push in Settings → Notifications to get alerts on your devices — this works from anywhere, including away from home.
For phone notifications at home, install the ntfy app and subscribe to your channel (shown in Settings → Notifications).

Rotate your ntfy channel anytime from Settings → Notifications if you think it's been shared or exposed; you'll need to re-subscribe in the ntfy app with the new channel afterward. LogCore also reminds you here once a channel is over 30 days old.
Proactive digests (morning summary, overdue alerts, weekly review) are configurable in Settings.

Want ntfy notifications away from home too, not just Web Push? An admin can give ntfy a public address if you're using a Cloudflare Tunnel: in Cloudflare Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → your tunnel → Public Hostname → Add, pick a subdomain (e.g. ntfy.yourdomain.com), and point it at http://localhost:5680. Then use that https:// address as the server in the ntfy app instead of your LAN address. This is optional — everything else works fine without it.
tips: ntfy is fully self-hosted — no third-party notification service is involved.
By default ntfy is only reachable on your server's local network; use Web Push for remote devices unless an admin has given ntfy a public hostname (see the howto above).
A channel ID is the only thing that gates who can read (or fake) your ntfy notifications, since ntfy topics have no login — rotating it immediately retires the old ID.

The moment ntfy gets a public hostname, launch.sh automatically locks down publishing to the app itself (an admin publisher token) while subscribing stays login-free — nothing extra to configure, and it fails safe (never silently breaks notifications) if that provisioning can't complete.

sections.title: Your Data & the Brain
sections.blurb: Everything you create is stored as plain Markdown and JSON files in your Brain. There's no database — the files are the source of truth, and they're yours.
howto: Export your entire Brain as a zip anytime from Settings → Account → Export Brain.
Because it's just files, any AI or text editor can read your Brain — no lock-in.
Admins can browse and edit raw Brain files under the Brain page.
tips: Self-hosting means your data stays on your server; it only leaves when you export or explicitly share it.
Back up your Brain folder regularly — it contains everything.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.blurb: LogCoreOS holds your whole life, so protecting it is the priority: your data stays isolated to you unless you deliberately share it, your password is never stored in a form anyone can read, and the app is built to keep intruders out. Here's what protects you — and, for the technically minded, exactly how.
howto: Your account is guarded by your password, which is stored only as a scrambled (hashed) value nobody can read or recover — so pick a strong, unique one; it's your main key.
After several wrong password guesses, sign-in for that account is paused for a few minutes. That blocks attackers trying huge lists of passwords, even from many computers at once.
Your data is private to you. Other people on the same instance cannot see your tasks, notes, money, or contacts unless you explicitly share them — and you can take that back anytime.
You can download everything you own at any time from Settings → Account → Export Brain. There is no lock-in.
Seeing a "too many attempts, try again later" message at sign-in means the protection is working — wait a few minutes, or ask an admin to reset your password.
tips: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed; sign-in runs in constant time, so response speed can't reveal which emails have accounts.
Login is defended on two layers — per-IP rate limiting AND a per-account temporary lockout (10 failed tries in 15 minutes) — so distributed credential-stuffing is stopped too.
Sessions use an HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure cookie (a JWT); logging out revokes it server-side. Keep COOKIE_SECURE=true on any HTTPS deployment.

Responses carry a Content-Security-Policy, HSTS (over HTTPS), X-Frame-Options: DENY and nosniff; page content is rendered escaped (no raw HTML), and your Brain text sent to the AI is wrapped to resist prompt injection.
Cross-user access is enforced on the server only — a record you have no relationship to simply isn't found; the browser never decides who can see what.

Self-host hardening: the app refuses to start on a default SECRET_KEY, talks to Docker only through a restricted socket-proxy, can require GPG-signed updates (UPDATE_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=true), and supports encrypted backups. Found a flaw? See SECURITY.md — please disclose privately to support@logcoretech.com.

sections.title: Appearance & Settings
sections.blurb: Make LogCore yours: theme, accent colour, background, density, and the shortcuts on your phone's bottom bar.
howto: In Settings, set light/dark/system mode, an accent colour, a background, density, and corner style.
Pin up to four modules per workspace to the mobile bottom bar under Shortcuts.
Set your timezone and session length so schedules and logins behave the way you expect.
tips: Appearance settings are saved to your account and follow you across devices.

sections.title: Admin
sections.blurb: Admin-only controls for the whole instance: users, roles, workspaces, and integrations. Reached from Settings → Admin Settings, not a separate menu item.
howto: Open Settings → Admin Settings → Users & Roles to add users, set role (admin/member), workspaces, and per-user module access — tap a user for their own page.
Create feature roles (e.g. cleaner, crew) from Users & Roles → Role Definitions to control which modules groups of users can see.
Configure the AI provider and web search from Admin Settings → AI — AI Usage & Limits (instance/personal/business totals + per-user daily/weekly/monthly caps) is on the same page.
Configure hosting, managed hosting, n8n, and Home Assistant from Admin Settings → Hosting; bank connections live on the Household/Team pages.
Grant "Can manage" on Household/Team pools from a user's own page in Users & Roles.

Deleting a user who owns items already shared with someone else opens a review page — choose per item whether it transfers to another user, transfers to the household/team pool, or is deleted, before the account can be removed.
tips: The first registered user becomes admin; after that, registration is closed by default so accounts are added deliberately.

faq.q: How do I get the AI to actually do things for me?
faq.a: Open Chat and ask in plain language. In the default Approve mode the AI reads your Brain freely and, whenever it wants to make a change, pauses and shows it to you — nothing happens until you click Approve.

faq.q: Where is my data stored? Is it private?
faq.a: Everything lives as plain Markdown and JSON files in your Brain, on your own server. There's no external database. Your data only leaves when you export it or explicitly share it with someone.

faq.q: How do I export or back up everything?
faq.a: Settings → Account → Export Brain downloads your entire Brain as a zip. Because it's just files, you can also back up the Brain folder directly on the server.

faq.q: What's the difference between the Personal and Business workspaces?
faq.a: They're fully separate spaces with their own data, modules, and priorities. If you have both, switch with the toggle in the sidebar. Nothing crosses between them automatically.

faq.q: Why can't I see a module another user has?
faq.a: Modules can be turned on or off per user, per workspace, and per feature role by an admin. Some modules are also workspace-specific (Journal, Household, and Home Assistant are personal; Team is business).

faq.q: How does task priority scoring work?
faq.a: Each task is scored from your life-priority order (set in Profile), its priority level, and urgency (overdue and due-today rank highest). The Dashboard shows the top 3 that result.

faq.q: What do Read, Contribute, and Edit mean when I share something?
faq.a: Read = view only. Contribute = a limited set of adds/edits you choose (for example, submit expenses only). Edit = full control including re-sharing. Sharing personal items sends a request the other person accepts or declines.

faq.q: How do I get notifications on my phone?
faq.a: Enable web push in Settings → Notifications for alerts anywhere, including away from home. For phone notifications at home, install the ntfy app and subscribe to your channel shown in Settings — ntfy is self-hosted and by default only reachable on your local network, so no third-party service is involved. If you want ntfy away from home too, an admin can give it a public address through your Cloudflare Tunnel (see the howto in this section) — LogCore automatically locks down who can publish once that's done, so subscribing stays just as simple. If you ever think your ntfy channel ID has leaked, rotate it from the same Settings card.

faq.q: Do I need n8n or Home Assistant to use LogCore?
faq.a: No. n8n Automation and Home Assistant are optional integrations. Everything else works without them.

faq.q: I found a bug or have an idea. How do I tell you?
faq.a: See Contact & Support at the bottom of this page — email support@logcoretech.com with what happened (and steps to reproduce for bugs). We read everything.

faq.q: Is my data private? Can other people on this instance see it?
faq.a: No. Everything you create lives in your own space and is private to you. Someone else can only see an item if you deliberately share it with them, and you can revoke that anytime. Even admins, who manage the instance, don't get a window into your personal tasks, notes, journal, money, or contacts unless you share them. See the Security & Privacy help section for the details.

faq.q: I keep getting "too many attempts" when I try to log in.
faq.a: That's the brute-force protection working: after several wrong passwords, sign-in for your account is paused for a few minutes to shut out attackers. Wait a bit and try again with the correct password, or ask an admin to reset it — it clears on its own.

support.note: Found a bug, want a feature, or have a complaint? Email us and we'll take a look. For bug reports, include what you did, what you expected, and what happened (a screenshot helps a lot).

highlights: Another round of security hardening: closed a request-forgery gap in SimpleFIN bank-connection setup, fixed a link-safety gap in AI chat, and stopped a few admin screens from showing raw internal error details. Updated several backend dependencies — including the file-upload handling library — to patch known security advisories. Also improved secrets storage for managed hosting instances.
Fixed a remaining AI Chat layout issue on mobile — the message box could sit higher than it should with empty space below it. It now sits where it should.

A round of AI Chat polish: fixed a layout issue where the page could appear shifted upward with empty space at the bottom, the sidebar's module list now scrolls on its own if you have enough modules enabled to fill the screen, and a saved conversation from the Business workspace could fail to reopen — now fixed.

If an update ever silently stops applying on an instance that already has a domain configured under Admin → Hosting, that's now fixed for good — the startup check that could get an already-working instance permanently stuck now trusts your configured domain instead. A few other small polish items too: clearer Privacy Policy and Terms of Service links during sign-up, and the version shown in the API docs now always matches what's actually installed.

Finance now has a real Transfer type — move money between two books, even across personal and business (or between two accounts in the same book), and both sides stay linked without ever counting as income or expense. Household and Team can also connect a joint/family bank account directly to the pool, and Finance now remembers the last book you had open, per workspace.

Every user's own contact is now permanently visible to their whole household and business team, from either workspace, with a green/red online dot and a click-for-last-seen popover — no separate share step needed. New contacts default to shared with your household/team too (with a "keep this personal" option), and any contact can be flipped to also show up in your other workspace. Admins can link a new user account to an existing household contact right when creating it. Contacts also sort alphabetically with an A-Z jump strip, can be deleted from their edit screen, and a personal contact can be converted into a shared household/team contact (single or bulk).

Company contacts now get their own fields — Locations and Hours — instead of personal fields like gender or career, and can have their own custom fields, set up from a new Settings → Admin Settings → Contact Fields screen.

Core Values are now individual pills instead of one comma-separated field. Career history lets you add a past role directly with its own start and end dates, not just by ending your current role — past roles can be edited afterward and list with the most recent one first. Your own profile's sensitive sections (Personal, Address, Career, Family, Values & Principles, Priorities) can each be hidden from your household/team with a toggle only you can set.

Tasks are now one flat, ranked list instead of grouped by category, with a new Sort by control (Priority, Date/Time, or Alphabetical) — the same control was also added to the Top 3 Tasks and Due Today dashboard blocks. A task's due time now shows right next to its due date. Fixed tasks and goals showing a red "OVERDUE" badge hours before they were actually due, for anyone west of UTC.

AI Chat now runs in the background — send a message and keep going, get notified when it's ready or needs your approval, and switch between multiple conversations that each keep working independently. The Chats list opens a conversation directly on click, with a live dot for one still working and an unread mark for one you haven't seen yet. Your message is saved the instant you send it (so it's never lost), the "Thinking…" indicator survives a reload, notifications are quieter when you're already watching, a paused approval/question/plan card survives leaving and coming back, and two real crashes (an "unexpected role" error after approving a card, and a full page crash when asking the AI to resize a dashboard block) are fixed. The AI can also now see and work with notes shared with you, not just your own, and reopens your last conversation per workspace.

Dashboard blocks can now have their own buttons — an Open button per row, or one-click status buttons on Tasks/Assets blocks — each with its own color, and now always aligned to the right consistently (two separate alignment bugs, fixed). Each block's card background and header can now be toggled on or off individually (both default on), and the AI can adjust those settings — plus a block's size and position — when building or editing a dashboard for you. An open dashboard also now picks up changes made elsewhere on its own every so often.

A dashboard can now be flagged to show up in both your personal and business workspaces instead of just the one it was created in, and reopening the Dashboard module returns you to whichever dashboard you had open last (within 30 minutes). Fixed a "Dashboard not found" error that showed on every first open of the module, a stale dashboard sticking around after switching workspaces, and a team dashboard created via the AI in chat immediately showing as not found.

Assets can now be created blank, without picking a template first, with their own typed custom fields — pick from the same six field types (text, number, date, yes/no, dropdown, contact) the admin Template editor uses — and a "Save as template" button turns those fields into a real, reusable template. Fixed those same custom fields not showing up anywhere outside of edit mode. Asset attachment images now open in a full-screen viewer instead of a new tab.
You can now pin your favorite modules to the desktop sidebar, the same way mobile already lets you pin shortcuts to its bottom bar — same settings screen and list, now shown on desktop too.
The Notes "···" menu and every other Notes dialog now open centered on screen, matching the rest of the app.

Fixed two mobile bugs where typing into a field (Notes/Journal, the Core Values field, an Assets custom-field dropdown, and a couple of others found along the way) zoomed the whole page in, and a bug where taps could land inches off target after the on-screen keyboard closed.

Diagnosed a push-notification delivery report — Web Push was already fully built and firing, with a likely fix now shipped (a real VAPID contact address instead of a placeholder) and clearer error messages for anyone still not receiving them.
Custom Dashboards — build unlimited, freeform dashboards from 30+ live data blocks across every module, with reusable templates, real record pickers, and full drag/resize on both desktop and mobile.

Profile is now your own Contact — one unified, photo-enabled profile shared across personal and business, with a real resume-style Work & Career section and better pickers for height/weight/blood type.
AI usage counter + caps — see instance-wide and per-user AI usage, with configurable daily/weekly/monthly limits and a live indicator right in Chat.

The AI can now build and edit your Dashboards directly from chat, ask a clarifying question when something's ambiguous, and reliably do exactly what an approved change showed — no more re-guessing after you click Approve.
AI Chat has a sleeker look — real formatting in replies, an auto-growing message box, and a consolidated toolbar with a single Memory pill.
Settings and Admin merged into one drill-down menu, and deleting a user with shared items now opens a review page instead of a blind confirm.
Dozens of mobile layout fixes across Tasks, Chat, Journal, Calendar, Household, and more, plus Notes archiving.

Mobile footer nav fixed for good — the bottom navigation on the installed home-screen app no longer floats above the true screen edge with a gap showing through; this was a standalone-app-only iOS rendering quirk, now resolved.
Atomic updates — updating now installs exactly the published release, never in-progress work that landed after it, so every instance on the same version runs the same code.

Reliable updates — the updater now refuses to report success when it couldn't actually fetch new code, recovers automatically if a past update didn't record its version, and the Admin → Updates card clearly shows what went wrong when an update fails.
Mobile polish — the Finance "＋ New book" button is back on screen, the Saved Chats panel no longer hides its header behind the notch, and the bottom navigation sits flush with the screen edge.
Rotate your notification channel — Settings → Notifications now has a Rotate button and a reminder when your channel is over 30 days old.
Safer push notifications — self-hosters exposing ntfy publicly can now require authentication for publishing while subscribing stays effortless.
Major security hardening — login lockout against password-guessing, stricter browser protections (CSP and more), locked-down automation APIs, and a safer Docker setup for self-hosters.
New Help → Security & Privacy section — how your account and data are protected, in plain language and technical detail.

Deals, assets, invoices, and money now link together — attach assets to a deal, see a Job P&L (invoiced, collected, expenses, net), create a pre-filled invoice from a Won deal, and jump between everything.
Asset pages show Finance activity (income / expenses / net), and contacts get a References card with every asset, invoice, and dollar tied to them.
Update flow fixes — the post-update What's New announcement fires reliably and the Updates card's refresh button checks for real.
In-app Help & Guide — press ? anywhere, or tap the ⓘ on any page. The AI reads the same guide, so just ask it how anything works.
Faster first-time setup — one page instead of three; Life Priorities start from a sensible default you can tune in Profile.
Your setup choice (Personal or Business) now shapes the whole instance — the workspace you didn't pick stays off until an admin enables it.
Mobile polish — the header no longer hides behind the notch on phones.
Smoother self-hosting — launch.sh works as root on a fresh VPS and accepts your Cloudflare Tunnel token directly.
New Finance module — books, accounts, bank sync, budgets, recurring bills, invoicing, and sharing with tight controls.
New Contacts (CRM) module — people and companies with interaction timelines, a deals pipeline, and follow-up reminders.
Goals overhaul — timeline filter, mandatory target dates, and completed goals stay until you clear them.
Share notes and folders with people, your household/team, or a role.
